title: Casting Out Nines: Practical Arithmetic Verification

problemStatement.formal: For any base b and modulus d with b % d = 1, digit sums respect addition and multiplication modulo d; failed digit-sum checks prove the claimed arithmetic result is wrong.
problemStatement.plain: Formalizes casting out nines and its base/modulus generalizations: digit sums mirror addition and multiplication modulo d when b % d = 1, enabling arithmetic verification and error detection.
whyMatters: Gives a machine-checked version of a classical hand-calculation verification method.
Shows the casting-out principle is a general modular-arithmetic fact, not only a base-10 trick.

proven: digit_sum_add_general and digit_sum_mul_general prove the base/modulus transfer laws.
detect_add_error_general and detect_mul_error_general prove the error-detection contrapositives.
casting_nines_add and casting_nines_mul specialize the result to base 10 modulo 9.
octal, hexadecimal, and modulo-3 specializations are included as concrete applications.
consistent_with_parent_div9 and consistent_with_parent_div3 connect the file back to the parent digit-sum congruence.
